claims: n-179-candidate.yaml is a packing.squares:Witness/v2 file (corners, rational scalars, 179 squares) whose exact rational side, rounded up at 12 places, #954 prints as the bound, 13.881367160110. Its exact coordinates were produced by this repository's packing-witness promote --strategy robust-rational at 591644a9 from the lab's decimal pose, n-179-decimal-pose.yaml, with center_dilation '1' and no dilation: pairs separated by at least about 2e-13, the squares that set the left wall, the bottom wall and the side touching them exactly, and other squares near a wall clearing it by up to about 1e-12. An upper bound only: no KKT, local-optimality, rigidity or global-optimality claim.

n179-witness.json is the same file as JSON. packing-witness-verify.txt is the author's run of this repository's packing-witness verify at 591644a9 on the witness placed under packing/witnesses/known-best/ (VERIFIED, exact-algebraic, 15931 pairs); sqcheck-output.txt is the author's run of verifier/sqcheck.py, an exact checker the source says was written separately from this repository's code (VALID, exact rational, the exact side rounded up at 15 places). The issue says sqcheck.py also certified the decimal pose in interval arithmetic at its own side before promotion. Those statements are the author's; no source program ran here.

The issue and README say the packing was found by an AI-run band-design search, new for this filing: tilted squares from a registry packing of the same family laid along the diagonal as a seed band; simulated annealing in a reduced model in which the tilted squares move freely and the axis-parallel squares sit on the two wall-anchored staircase lattices, present or absent, with the overlap of the squares that must be kept as energy; then one quench with Evan Daniel's ALM+SLP code from evand/square-packing search/packer at bb4cc78e, MIT. The band is built from the tilted squares of the registry's n = 70 packing (Ryan Xu, found_by; improved by Evan Daniel and PingYou Ltd; side 8.880960371555579595), a two-row band of 20 squares at -40.7505 degrees along the diagonal; the registry's n = 207 packing (PingYou Ltd) is two such bands, mirrored. Seed M_55_16_36: that band where x + y <= 16, a second copy shifted by (5, 5) where x + y > 16, overlapping squares dropped, random adjacent squares added up to 36 tilted squares; annealed at side 13.8812 (2e6 moves, energy 0.084), then quenched to 13.881367160110; two other seeds of the same scan (cuts 12 and 15, 35 tilted squares) quench to the same side. The result is one straight band of 35 squares from corner to corner (23 at -40.81 degrees, eight near -41.4 where the two copies join, four near -39.9 at the lower-left end), where the record's band is wavy and lies on the other diagonal. They report, against the registry packing matched by assignment up to the square's symmetries: 146 of 179 centres move by more than 1e-3, 54 by more than 0.05 (largest 0.886); 44 squares re-tilted by more than 1 degree (largest 44.36); 37 squares tilted by more than 0.5 degree against the record's 35. They ask that the improvement be credited to Doğa Özden, the band's source packing n = 70 and the current record to their holders as the registry lists them, and the local optimizer to Evan Daniel. The issue says the search and its code were written and run by AI agents and that the checks were run by code that did not produce the packing; the issue and repository were prepared and posted by Özden's AI agent, which uses the account kenaznia-doga; Özden directed the work.
